skill.name: happyhorse-1-0
skill.description: Generate short text-to-video clips with HappyHorse 1.0 through the RunComfy CLI. The skill documents model options, prompt guidance, supported aspect ratios, RunComfy setup, and output handling.
skill.summary: Run HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video jobs on RunComfy with model-specific prompt guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The real risks are the intended RunComfy CLI executions, global setup commands, and the disclosed POST to the RunComfy Model API. Most other static findings are Markdown backtick, REST ellipsis, documentation link, or standard credential-store false positives.

remediation.issue: Local CLI and package-manager commands are part of normal use.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user confirmation before install, login, or generation commands, and document how to verify the RunComfy CLI package.

remediation.issue: Prompts and bearer-token authenticated requests are sent to RunComfy.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the outbound endpoint disclosure prominent and remind users not to submit sensitive prompt data unless approved.

remediation.issue: Generated files are downloaded into a user-selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a dedicated output directory and preserve the documented host whitelist and file-size cap.

content.value_statement: Creating short AI videos requires model-specific prompt structure and CLI setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video generation on RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit HappyHorse video requests to the RunComfy text-to-video endpoint.
Documents supported aspect ratios, resolution choices, duration limits, seeds, and watermark options.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for default, vertical, and lower-cost test generations.
Explains prompt tactics for motion, camera direction, multi-shot consistency, and audio direction.
Documents RunComfy setup, exit codes, token storage, network endpoints, and output downloads.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and valid authentication.
Uses a hosted RunComfy Model API, so prompts and outputs leave the local machine.
Supports text-to-video only in this template, not image-to-video or reference-video input.
Limits clips to 15 seconds and the five documented aspect ratios.

use_cases.title: Create Brand Story Clips
use_cases.description: Build short product or brand scenes with consistent characters, camera direction, and synchronized ambience.

use_cases.title: Produce Vertical Social Videos
use_cases.description: Prepare platform-native 9:16 clips with duration, watermark, resolution, and audio guidance set before generation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Cinematic Sequences
use_cases.description: Draft multi-shot video prompts that restate character anchors and keep each visual beat clear.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple text-to-video generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short HappyHorse 1.0 video prompt for this idea: [idea]. Use default 16:9, 1080P, and five seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Vertical Short
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for social video settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this concept into a vertical HappyHorse 1.0 RunComfy request: [concept]. Include aspect ratio, duration, watermark preference, and audio direction.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Two-Shot Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for character consistency across shots.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-shot HappyHorse 1.0 prompt with strong character consistency for [story]. Keep within 15 seconds and explain the settings.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Video Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across related RunComfy video models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare HappyHorse 1.0 with Wan 2.7, Seedance 2, and LTX 2 for [project]. Recommend the model, settings, and prompt structure.

output_examples.input: A designer asks for a five-second 16:9 product reveal.
output: Recommended HappyHorse 1.0 with 1080P output and a five-second duration.
Prompt revised to describe product motion, camera movement, lighting, and ambient audio.
RunComfy output directory guidance included for the generated video file.

output_examples.input: A social media manager needs a vertical cafe clip without watermark.
output: Prepared a 9:16 short-form prompt with an eight-second duration.
Added close-up camera language, cafe ambience, and steam motion details.
Included the watermark preference as a generation setting.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker wants two connected shots with the same character.
output: Structured the scene into two clear shots with repeated wardrobe and identity anchors.
Added location, motion, and audio continuity for both shots.
Flagged the 15-second limit and suggested keeping one visual beat per shot.

best_practices: Describe motion over time, including actions, camera movement, and audio cues.
Keep each clip focused on one visual beat before adding more shots.
Reuse clear character and wardrobe anchors when asking for multi-shot consistency.
anti_patterns: Do not submit static image descriptions when the goal is believable video motion.
Do not mix conflicting visual styles, camera directions, or audio instructions.
Do not request unsupported durations, aspect ratios, or external audio-driven lip-sync.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the hosted RunComfy Model API through the local RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and either login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it create longer videos?
faq.answer: No. The documented endpoint supports clips from 3 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Can it use images or reference video?
faq.answer: No. This template covers text-to-video only. Image-to-video requires a separate pipeline.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated output files into the output directory chosen for the run.

faq.question: Does it send prompts to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts are sent to RunComfy over HTTPS for hosted model processing.
